findings.quote: .metaproject-filters-pop { display: grid; gap: var(--sp-2); padding: var(--sp-2) var(--sp-3) var(--sp-3); }
findings.problem: Filters popover is clipped by 51 px at the 720x480 minimum window when the stale banner is expanded, and cannot scroll. The popover is a fixed-position .menu whose top is computed once as anchor.bottom + 4 (MetaprojectView.tsx FiltersPopover: `setPosition({ left, top: rect.bottom + 4 })`). The only height limit is the shared .menu max-block-size of 400px, a fixed number, not a function of the room below the anchor. The rule above adds no max-block-size or overflow clamp tied to the window, so when the anchor sits low the popover runs past the window edge. Its content (229 px) is below 400 px, so it never becomes scrollable either and the last row is unreachable.
findings.impact: At the smallest supported window (720x480), a developer with a stale graph who opens Details and then Filters cannot reach the lower relationship-type chips, the symbol-layer reason or Reset filters. A stale graph is the state the flow journal calls the one a developer is in most of the time. Any state that pushes the header down further (a longer reason, a second banner, a larger text scale) moves the cut up. The position is computed once on open, so a resize while it is open is not tracked (unmeasured).
findings.suggested_fix: Bound the popover by the room below its anchor: compute `maxHeight = window.innerHeight - top - 8` next to `top` in FiltersPopover and set `max-block-size: min(400px, that)` with `overflow-y: auto`; or flip it above the anchor when there is more room there. Re-measure at 720x480 with Details expanded: popover bottom at or below 472 and scrollHeight greater than clientHeight.
findings.evidence: Orchestrator live probe, browser dev build, 720x480, dark, Graph, 'Agent Bus', depth 1, getBoundingClientRect (research-evidence/live-filters-popover-720x480.txt). One-line banner: button bottom 225, popover top 232 bottom 455, 25 px of room, not cut. Banner with Details expanded (banner 122 px): button bottom 301, popover top 308 bottom 531, window 480, cut by 51 px; scrollHeight equals clientHeight (229), so no scroll; the 'Not available: ...' note and the lower chips are outside the window. Not measured: light theme, 1180x780 and 1440x900 with the popover open, the native Tauri window, window resize while open. Measured by the orchestrator in two engines at 720x480 with the freshness Details expanded: Chromium 156, popover bottom 531 against a 480 px window, cut by 51 px, no scroll (.metaproject/reviews/2026-11-23-review-flow-branch/research-evidence/live-filters-popover-720x480.txt); system WKWebView (AppleWebKit 605.1.15, macOS 26.7.3), layout box bottom 497, cut by 17 px, no scroll (.metaproject/reviews/2026-11-23-review-flow-branch/research-evidence/verify-F-001-3.txt). With the one-line banner it fits in both (.metaproject/reviews/2026-11-23-review-flow-branch/research-evidence/verify-F-001-2.txt). The height cap the reviewer calls max-block-size 400px is `.menu`'s `max-height: min(420px, calc(100vh - 80px))` (styles.css:143), which is 400 px at this window height. Normalisation notes: confidence was not stated by the reviewer and is set at normalisation; the same defect was raised by review-ui-ux (review-ui-ux-w2, UX-001, minor); the same defect was raised by review-ui-ux (review-ui-ux-w1, UX-002, info).

findings.problem: The explorer root `<section className="flows metaproject">` becomes a size container. container-type inline-size applies layout containment, and an element with layout containment is the containing block of its `position: fixed` descendants. The Filters popover (`FiltersPopover` in MetaprojectView.tsx, rendered inside that section, class `menu`, which `styles.css` sets to `position: fixed`) is placed with viewport coordinates from `anchor.getBoundingClientRect()` (`left`, `top: rect.bottom + 4`). With the new container, those values are resolved against the section's padding box, not the viewport, so the popover is shifted by the section's own viewport offset (sidebar width, toolbar height) and the Escape/outside-press logic and the horizontal clamp to `window.innerWidth` no longer match where it is drawn.
findings.impact: Where the section is not at viewport (0,0) the Filters popover opens displaced from its button, and can fall partly outside the window. The only live measurement (720x480) shows the popover top 3 px below the 4 px the code intends (button bottom 225, popover top 232), which is consistent with a small offset, but no measurement was taken with the sidebar visible (1180x780, 1440x900) or in the native window.
findings.suggested_fix: Render the popover through a portal to document.body (the other `.menu` users are not inside a size container), or move the container off the ancestor of the popover (for example put `container-type` on `.metaproject-panes`, and leave the header, banner and popover outside it), or compute the position relative to `root.current.getBoundingClientRect()`. Add a DOM-free check or a live probe at 1180x780 with the popover open that compares popover.left to anchor.right - 320.
findings.evidence: Read: metaproject.css line `.metaproject { container: metaproject / inline-size; }` (slice-06, hunk 1); MetaprojectView.tsx:171-201 (FiltersPopover, fixed-position `.menu` placed from getBoundingClientRect, rendered at :684 inside the section opened at :730); styles.css:142-143 (`.menu { position: fixed; ... }`); research-evidence/live-filters-popover-720x480.txt (top 232 vs button bottom 225). CSS Containment: container-type size/inline-size applies layout containment, which makes the element a containing block for fixed descendants. Not run: read-only tools and no browser, so the displacement is derived from the spec and the code, not measured at a width where the sidebar is visible. Measured by the orchestrator after the finding was raised: in Chromium 156 (.metaproject/reviews/2026-11-23-review-flow-branch/research-evidence/live-filters-popover-containing-block.txt) and in the system WKWebView, AppleWebKit 605.1.15 on macOS 26.7.3 (.metaproject/reviews/2026-11-23-review-flow-branch/research-evidence/verify-F-002-2.txt), the popover's layout box sits exactly at its inline viewport coordinates (displacement 0, 0) while the section's origin is (60, 77), so neither engine makes the size container the containing block of the fixed popover. Not measured: WebKit of older macOS versions. review-regression (wave 3) noted the same possibility without filing it.

findings.problem: FiltersPopover registers on the app-wide Escape stack (components/ui.tsx:44-70: window keydown listener, `e.preventDefault(); top.current?.()` for the top entry) and so makes `overlayOpen()` true (ui.tsx:81). On base the explorer was unmounted when the user left the view, taking any popover with it. On head the explorer is mounted but hidden (RetainedView), and `filtersOpen` is deliberately kept across view switches (comment 'Open or closed is explorer state ... survives a view or tab switch'). The only close paths are Escape, a mousedown outside, or the button. A keyboard user can Tab to the sidebar nav and press Enter (no mousedown, popover has no focus-out close) and arrive in another view with the popover open but hidden.
findings.impact: While that hidden popover is registered: the first Escape in the other view is consumed by it (preventDefault, then focuses a hidden anchor), so Escape does not reach the visible view; AppShell's view shortcuts back off (AppShell.tsx:84 and :112 return when overlayOpen()); App.tsx:360 and BrowserPanel.tsx:114 (`show = ... && !overlayOpen()`) also treat an overlay as open, so the native browser view hides. Nothing on screen explains it; a second Escape clears it. If true for you: minor (recoverable, needs the keyboard path described).
findings.suggested_fix: Close the popover when its view is hidden: pass the RetainedView `visible` flag into MetaprojectView and call setFiltersOpen(false) on becoming hidden, or mount FiltersPopover only while visible. Add a test that switches view with the popover open and checks overlayOpen() is false.
findings.evidence: Also described, without a finding, by review-regression (wave 2), which lists the overlayOpen() consumers it reaches: App.tsx:360, AppShell.tsx:84/112, BrowserPanel.tsx:114/130, ReviewBoard.tsx:247/258. findings.quote: const current = () => generation === project.current && shownSelection.current === from && activeMode.current === "wiki";
findings.problem: Concurrent wiki-link lookups are won by whichever read returns first
findings.impact: Trigger: click an unloaded wiki link A, then another unloaded link B on the same page before A's `search` read resolves. Both reads pass `current()` because the selection has not changed; whichever resolves first calls `openDocument` and changes the selection, after which the other is dropped. If A's read is the slower one, B opens (the last click wins); if A is faster, A opens and B is silently discarded. The outcome depends on read latency, not click order. No data is lost and the user can click again.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a lookup counter in a ref, increment it in openPath, and have `current()` also require `token === lookup.current` (the pattern `latestSearch.current.generation` already uses nearby).
findings.evidence: `const current = () => generation === project.current && shownSelection.current === from && activeMode.current === "wiki";` in openPath, which guards only against a changed project, selection or mode, not against a second lookup started from the same page. Normalisation notes: confidence was not stated by the reviewer and is set at normalisation; the quote was taken at normalisation from the code the reviewer cited.

findings.problem: Recorded OpenSpec scroll defect still live: choose() zeroes the content pane before the history entry is recorded. findings.impact: For a node with a self-edge (for example a wiki page whose `links` edge points at itself) the graph caption reads '0 incoming · 0 outgoing' while the panel fact reads '0 incoming · 1 outgoing', and the Relationships tab lists the node as its own outgoing neighbour, whose row selects the node already shown (a no-op). AC7 asks for the panel counts to come from the root-adjacent edges, so the panel follows the criterion; the caption is the one that differs.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one rule for both: skip self-loops in groupRelationships (the row does nothing useful), or count them in layoutNeighborhood. Skipping them in groupRelationships keeps the two counts equal.
findings.evidence: RelationshipList.tsx groupRelationships: `if (edge.from === projection.root) adjacent.outgoing.push(...)` runs before any self-loop test; graphLayout.ts lines 505-508: `if (edge.from === edge.to) return; if (edge.to === root.id) incoming++; if (edge.from === root.id) outgoing++;`. The self-loop case is only reachable if the producer emits a self-edge; not verified that it does.
